hook: A colony of bacteria goes from $3$ thousand to $192$ thousand in six hours. On an ordinary graph, the first hours are squashed against the axis and you cannot see what is happening. Put the vertical axis on a logarithmic scale and the same data fall on a straight line, which tells you at a glance that the growth is exponential.

prereq.q: On a logarithmic scale, the labels $1$, $10$, $100$ are equally spaced. What does each step do?
An exponential model $y = a \cdot b^x$ has $b = 1.5$. What happens to $y$ when $x$ increases by $1$?

figure.caption: The data $y = 3 \cdot 2^t$ (thousands) on a logarithmic vertical axis: equal steps in time are equal factors, so the points lie on a line.

chain.effect: $\log y = \log a + x\log b$, a linear function of $x$

chain.cause: Plot $\log y$, or use a logarithmic vertical axis
chain.effect: the data lie on a straight line: a semi-log plot

chain.cause: Read the line's slope and intercept
chain.effect: slope $= \log b$ and intercept $= \log a$, so $b = 10^{\text{slope}}$ and $a = 10^{\text{intercept}}$
they are not exponential of the form $a \cdot b^x$ (linear data bend down; a vertical shift bends too)

ideas: A semi-log plot has one axis (usually the vertical one) on a logarithmic scale with some base $n > 1$.
Exponential data $y = a \cdot b^x$ look linear on it, because $\log_n y = \log_n a + x\log_n b$.
From the line: $b = n^{\text{slope}}$ and $a = n^{\text{intercept}}$. With a natural-log scale, use $e$.
A function with a vertical shift, $a \cdot b^x + k$ with $k \ne 0$, does not give a line.

misconception.wrong: A line on a semi-log plot means the data are linear, so the slope is the amount added each step.
misconception.right: The vertical scale shows $\log y$. A line means $\log y$ is linear, so $y$ is exponential: the slope is $\log b$, and each step multiplies $y$ by $b$.

summary: A semi-log plot puts one axis on a logarithmic scale. Exponential data $y = a \cdot b^x$ then fall on a straight line, because $\log y = \log a + x\log b$. The slope of the line is $\log b$ and its intercept is $\log a$, so you can read the model's growth factor and starting value from the line. Linear data, or exponential data with a vertical shift, bend instead.
